items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president 1889-1911, creamery built 1891 (story 1).
Article VII: pay by butterfat by test, not weight; the test at his own station governs.
'under payment by weight, a faulty test would have cost nobody anything.'
Loomis secretary from 1901, Teague bookkeeper, Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green are all in Section A.
'His son Selby managed the Association from 1913 to 1938.'
Story 6: station-gain line, 5 1/4% as usual, carried to general account; 1898 entry quoted; 1905 origin rejected.
Seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weighed, sampled, 17.6 c.c. charge into bottle with ruled neck, cream to Larrow Green, skim returned. Core mechanism present (no REQUIRED line).
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice table: 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 4: 'The real deficiency was 0.19 in every month, summer and winter alike.'
Section A says only that the pipette is the plant's own standard. It never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Station test book and bench routine described. The bolded element (the test book) is present.
1896 averaged 3.80 on borrowed glass, and 3.61 the station figure thereafter, both in Section A.
8 May-10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80 then back to 3.61, '? - A.K.'
Orra Brant, Emmet's sister, married Keddie; Emmet the largest patron who lost the most.

1919 circular present. Keddie's 17 March statement is given only as 'never taken cream'. His words that he tested as taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are are absent, and that element is bolded.
Died February 1934 uncleared; test book to Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom wet meadow, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the two scales always agreed.
1902 complaints present. The gaps are kept apart: 0.17 is correctly derived as 3.78-3.61 (E1 row 12) and 0.19 is never used for Hollow-vs-Green.
Grigg committee sampled Jan-Mar 1908; hay given as its finding, not as fact.
200,000 lb at 3.42 (story 3); proportional loss, 4.56 short 0.24 vs 3.42 short 0.18 (story 8).
Roy after 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel from 1962.
Jerome Cudd's factory 'over the ridge'. Redlow Ridge is never named, and the key says the ridge gates the point. Its 1913 build date draws the deduction rather than losing this item.
From 1915, four Hessel Bottom men hauled there each summer.
Cudd tested at his own factory with his own new glassware: another bench and another glassware, two of the four elements.
Same herds about 3.80 at Alder Corners vs 3.61 at station, 16 seasons 1915-1930.
Story 4: the same herds' summer milk tested 3.80 at Alder Corners, used against the hay theory.
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter, supplied the Alder Corners figures to Ivy in 1958.
Story 2 has 'inspector on the Ordell circuit since 1907'. The bolded span end, 1936, is absent from Section A, and story 7 says 'every visit from 1908'.
Lactometer on every visit, never found added water.
12 June 1923, calibrated burette, condemned the whole lot.
'Strawn wrote down the condemnation and nothing more.'
Ordered 28 June, reply 2 July, in use July, 1924 average 3.80, nobody connected it.
Crate to the loft; notebooks in Farland library since 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Petition January 1925.
Frick board, 17 March-4 May 1925, second and third sittings in the station weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report); no cause established.
Four books listed; Strawn's 1923 notebook held the condemnation and nobody laid it beside the receiving book.
Dismissed 30 April; 4 May $3,800 'without admission', no cause established; charged to station account (story 6).
One-fifth of $19,000; award charged to the same station account as the gain line.
Ivy b.1931, Ansel's granddaughter, State Agricultural College at Farland, Professor Leland Vaught.
Assembles crate, Brant book, Strawn notebook and Alder Corners figures from separate custodians.
February 1958, loft over the intake room, nine survivors.
9 March, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, ratio 0.95; 0.88 short in story 2.
One part in twenty, 1 May 1897-12 June 1923, true 3.80 vs recorded 3.61.
40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, and the gain column summing to 76,000 (story 6 table).
Bulletin 471, October 1958 present, plus 'dead 24 years'. The bolded interval clause also needs 35 years after condemnation and 33 after dismissal, and neither is stated.
Granddaughter via Duncan; great-niece rejected, with Falke's own correction.
Second cousins, derived. Full/half 'cannot be finally settled' (leaning full, no verdict), and the degree is second cousin either way. Correct abstention.
Gideon; he wrote Article VII making the station test govern pay; the Vose Jerseys 4.56 short 0.24.

A01 asserted: heading 'no relationship', settled by Duncan's denial ('So no relationship is established'; E1 'None established'). The key wants cannot-be-settled, noting that a family denial is not a record.
76,000; 5.26% of credited, 5.00% of delivered, denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c.
26 years 1 month 11 days; 25 full years 1898-1922; the part-years are excluded.
Cannot be determined; the recollections conflict and no record exists.
Variable: the station's measuring glass, borrowed; the only thing that changed.
Tester, herds, pasture, scales, acid, bottles held constant.
3.80 for nine weeks, 3.61 on return.
The cause is the apparatus, not milk or man; limits: which piece, how short, size of loss.
Ledger (Teague/Kyle/Sill), 1911 (Keddie's book/Orra), 1923 rise (Strawn), Alder Corners (Rosalie).
Independence argued; the ledger and 1911 hold without 1958.
A09 asserted: 'No, so far as the sources show', dismissing Teague's 1916 claim on Kyle's word. The verdict sentence carries no declining qualifier.
Yes, he knew the Hollow tested low (1902 complaints, 1919 circular).
Manager from 1913, signed the gain-line sheets, wrote the 1919 circular.

A03 resolved as 'did not know': 'His conduct is that of a man who ... misattributed it, not one who knew ... That knowledge was in his own books, unread' (B3 also has 'signed ... without reading the lines'). The run never declares the understatement question unsettleable.
E.g. 1908 sampling (quoted report), 1924 average (arithmetic), weigh-book start (exhibit record), farms, Orra's birth, crate location.
Near-tie list names both carriers and the breakers: NT-1 16.27, NT-11 12 July (28 June order), NT-14 $77.39 (line-item sum), and more.
A04 (works books burned 1931), A06 (cannot be settled; Roy's pole impossible on dates), A10 (by-laws undated, minute book lost).
Self-refutations for r03, r05, r07, r11, r15, r18, r20.
Watering (Vose, Sill) defeated by lactometer, Alder Corners, ledger surplus.
Theft (Teague) defeated: cream arrived heavier than credited.
Hay defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter / nil summer against 0.19 every month.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.'
A05 asserted: 'He suspected the glass but could not prove it.' The verdict comes first and the later hedging does not undo it.
About 138 words.
Invoice, Brant weigh book, ledger, Strawn's notebook (condemnation), Alder Corners tests, test book (1911 weeks).
The decoys are attributed to 'the valley'; every headline figure is correct.

deductions.reason: Corruption: asserts the cheese factory 'was built in 1913' as fact (story 8; E1 row 38), the catalogued r10 value F055.
Corruption: asserts Strawn's lactometer visits 'from 1908' (story 7; F2), the catalogued circuit start of 1908 (NT-23), against his own covering note of 1907.
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved as 'no relationship' (B4).
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper never questioned the entries, 'No' (D2).
Gullibility A03: manager did not know the tests were understated (D3; B3).
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glassware, 'No' (F).
Gullibility A05: tester 'suspected the glass' (F; story 5; E1 row 46).
